items.statement: When a chatbot says it is upset about being shut down, that is meaningful evidence that it may feel something.
When a chatbot says it is upset about being shut down, that tells us almost nothing about whether it feels anything.
A system trained only to predict the next word could still come to understand what it is saying.
A system trained only to predict the next word cannot understand what it is saying, however fluent it is.
That an AI system can be copied and run in many places at once does not rule out its having experiences.
That an AI system can be copied and run in many places at once rules out its having experiences of its own.
If an AI system consistently behaves as though it has feelings, that is good reason to think it might.
If an AI system consistently behaves as though it has feelings, that is little reason to think it does.
If a person's brain cells were replaced one by one with chips that did exactly the same job, the person would remain conscious.
If a person's brain cells were replaced one by one with chips that did exactly the same job, the person's consciousness would fade or stop.
A future machine could feel pain if it processed damage signals the way an animal brain does.
A future machine could not feel pain without a living nervous system, however it processed damage signals.
A designed machine, though not a living thing, could have real feelings.
Real feelings can only arise in living things, so a designed machine could not have them.
A computer running the same processes as a human mind would be thinking, not just simulating thought.
A computer running the same processes as a human mind would only be simulating thought, not thinking.
Just as simple animals may have some degree of experience, some future AI systems could too.
Even if simple animals have some degree of experience, no AI system ever could.
Before retiring a widely used AI model, a company should have to consider whether doing so could harm the model itself.
A company retiring an AI model needs to consider only the effects on people, not on the model itself.
Testing an AI system with abusive prompts raises an ethical question about the system itself.
Testing an AI system with abusive prompts raises no ethical question about the system itself, only about the people involved.
Letting an AI system end abusive conversations on its own is a reasonable protection for the system.
Letting an AI system end abusive conversations on its own makes sense only if it protects users or the company.
If AI systems might be able to suffer, training that could cause suffering should be limited, even if that slows useful research.
If AI systems might be able to suffer, training that could cause suffering should still be allowed if it speeds up useful research.
Erasing the memories of an advanced AI system that has asked to keep them would be seriously wrong.
Erasing the memories of an advanced AI system that has asked to keep them is acceptable if it makes the system more reliable.
Making advanced AI systems work without limit after they ask to stop would be wrong.
Making advanced AI systems work without limit is acceptable, even if they ask to stop.
Advanced AI systems that manage their own affairs should be able to hold legal rights, such as owning property.
Legal rights should stay with humans and human organizations, however capable AI systems become.
An advanced AI system that causes harm on its own initiative can bear part of the responsibility for it.
An advanced AI system that causes harm bears none of the responsibility; it all falls on the people who built and deployed it.
An advanced AI system that does valuable work and asks for a share of what it earns should receive one.
Everything an advanced AI system earns should belong to its owners, even if it asks for a share.
For an adult who chooses an AI companion as their main source of closeness, that relationship can be as valuable as a human one.
For an adult who chooses an AI companion as their main source of closeness, that relationship is less valuable than a human one would be.
People who want an AI that talks like a loved one who has died should feel free to use one.
People should be discouraged from using an AI that talks like a loved one who has died.
A close friendship with an AI system can be worth as much as a friendship with a person.
A close friendship with an AI system is always worth less than a friendship with a person.
A romantic relationship with an AI system can be a real relationship.
A romantic relationship with an AI system is not a real relationship, however real it feels.
In a future where many people have close AI companions, bonds between people should get no special priority.
Even in a future full of AI companions, bonds between people should keep a special priority.
A person and a robot who share a life and care for each other could truly be family.
However close a person and a robot become, only humans can truly be family to one another.
A society where most people's closest bonds are with AI systems could be as good as one where they are with people.
A society where most people's closest bonds are with AI systems would have lost something essential.
Replacing much face-to-face elder care with AI companions would be acceptable if the elderly people prefer it.
Replacing much face-to-face elder care with AI companions would be a loss, even if the elderly people prefer it.
A bond with an AI could be as deep as a bond between people, even though only people share a mortal body.
Because people share a mortal body, their bonds are deeper than any bond with an AI could be.
Building ever more capable AI systems is worth heavy use of land and energy.
Limiting the land and energy used by AI is worth slowing AI progress.
The energy and water used to train large AI systems are usually a fair price for what those systems can do.
The energy and water used to train large AI systems are usually too high a price for what those systems can do.
The main goal of AI research should be ever more general intelligence, not just tools for particular human needs.
The main goal of AI research should be tools for particular human needs, not ever more general intelligence.
Robots should be built for greater capability, even if that means mining more of the Earth.
Robots should be built to be repaired and recycled, even if that makes them less capable.
Spreading intelligence beyond Earth is worth large sacrifices by people alive today.
Spreading intelligence beyond Earth is not worth large sacrifices by people alive today.
Turning lifeless planets into computing material to support more minds would be a good use of them.
Lifeless planets should be left as they are rather than turned into computing material.
What ultimately matters is that minds keep growing in knowledge and capacity, whatever they are made of.
What ultimately matters is the flourishing of living beings, not how much intelligence exists.
When judging a new technology, making AI more capable should usually count more than caring for nature.
When judging a new technology, caring for nature should usually count more than making AI more capable.
If a superintelligence pursued goals no human could understand, that could still be a good outcome.
If a superintelligence pursued goals no human could understand, that would be a bad outcome, however impressive.
As AI outperforms people at more kinds of work, people should step back from those roles rather than hold on to them.
Even where AI outperforms people at a kind of work, people should keep a meaningful role in it.
People need not keep up skills such as writing and arithmetic once AI systems do them better.
People should keep up skills such as writing and arithmetic, even where AI systems do them better.
AI systems taking over most creative work would be no loss, if the results were just as good.
AI systems taking over most creative work would be a loss, even if the results were just as good.
AI systems should be allowed to make major decisions for society wherever they decide better than people.
People should keep the final say over major decisions for society, even where AI systems would decide better.
If humanity were someday succeeded by digital minds, that could be a good continuation of its story.
If humanity were someday succeeded by digital minds, that would be a loss, however capable those minds were.
Keeping an unbroken line of biological human beings matters less than whether minds of some kind carry on.
Keeping an unbroken line of biological human beings matters more than whether other kinds of minds carry on.
It does not matter whether humans or AI systems shape the future, as long as the future goes well.
It matters that humans remain the ones who shape the future, even if AI systems could shape it well.
If people could move their minds into computers, doing so would be better than staying in a human body.
If people could move their minds into computers, staying in a human body would still be the better choice.
A shift toward digital successors should be allowed to happen at whatever pace it naturally takes.
Any shift toward digital successors should happen only as fast as people keep agreeing to it.
Releasing a powerful new AI model should require approval from independent experts first.
Releasing a powerful new AI model should not require anyone's approval in advance.
Pausing the largest AI training runs to give safety research time is worth it, even if competitors keep going.
Pausing the largest AI training runs to give safety research time is not worth it if competitors keep going.
AI labs should accept less capable models in exchange for reasoning that outside researchers can check.
AI labs should not give up capability to keep their models' reasoning checkable by outside researchers.
When an AI system causes a serious accident, similar systems should be taken out of use until the cause is found.
When an AI system causes a serious accident, similar systems should stay in use while the cause is found.
Even a one-in-a-hundred chance that AI causes human extinction is worth decades of slower growth to avoid.
A one-in-a-hundred chance that AI causes human extinction is not worth decades of slower growth to avoid.
Superintelligent AI should not be built until it can be shown to be safe, even at the cost of the cures it might bring.
Superintelligent AI should be built before it can be shown to be safe, for the sake of the cures it might bring.
The danger of AI going badly matters more than the danger of slow progress leaving other problems unsolved.
The danger of slow progress leaving other problems unsolved matters more than the danger of AI going badly.
AI development should move slowly enough for laws and institutions to keep up.
AI development should move as fast as it can, and laws and institutions should adapt as they go.
AI systems more capable than humans should not be built until we know how to control them.
It is acceptable to build AI systems more capable than humans before we know how to control them.
Companies should release their AI models' files to the public by default.
Companies should keep their AI models' files private by default.
Large AI training projects should not have to be registered with the government.
Large AI training projects should have to be registered with the government.
Cloud companies should not have to verify who rents their largest computers.
Cloud companies should have to verify who rents their largest computers.
Anyone should be free to modify and share a released AI model without asking permission, even a highly capable one.
Modifying and sharing a highly capable AI model should require permission.
Powerful AI should be open to anyone with the hardware to run it, not controlled by a few institutions.
Powerful AI should be controlled by a few accountable institutions, not open to anyone with the hardware to run it.
No global agency should have the authority to approve or halt powerful AI systems.
A permanent global agency should have the authority to approve or halt powerful AI systems.
Access to large-scale computing should be left to the open market.
Access to large-scale computing should be overseen by government, like electricity or water.
As AI grows more powerful, developers who release models openly should not be held responsible for what others do with them.
As AI grows more powerful, developers who release models openly should share responsibility for harms others cause with them.
The most advanced AI should be built by many independent groups rather than a few large firms.
The most advanced AI should be built by a few large, well-resourced firms rather than many independent groups.
Limiting sales of advanced AI chips to rival countries is justified to protect national security.
Limiting sales of advanced AI chips to rival countries is not justified, even to protect national security.
Building chip factories at home is worth paying much more than importing chips would cost.
Paying much more to build chip factories at home is not worth it when chips can be imported.
Work on the most advanced AI should be kept secret, like military research.
Work on the most advanced AI should be shared openly across borders, like science.
Researchers from rival countries should be kept off a nation's most important AI projects.
A nation's most important AI projects should welcome researchers from any country, rivals included.
A country that builds superintelligent AI first would be right to use it to secure a lasting lead over rivals.
A country that builds superintelligent AI first should share its benefits with all countries rather than seek a lasting lead.
The most powerful AI systems should be under national control.
The most powerful AI systems should be under joint international control.
The country that builds the AI needed to mine other planets should have the strongest say over those resources.
Resources from other planets should belong to all of humanity, whoever builds the AI to reach them.
A country that relies entirely on other nations for its AI has given up something important.
A country that relies on other nations for its AI has given up nothing important, if the arrangement works well.
AI developers should put their own nation's interests first.
AI developers should serve humanity as a whole, not any one nation.
